# Campeyyakkhandhaka (Kd 9)

**ID:** Kd 9
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Campeyyakkhandhaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul8.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Campeyyakkhandhaka* is the ninth chapter of the *Mahāvagga* in the Khandhaka division of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [Frauwallner 1956; von Hinüber 1996; Norman 1983]. In the *Cullavagga* account of the Second Council at Vaiśālī, the text is also cited as the *Campeyyaka Vinayavatthu* [von Hinüber 1996; Sung 1999]. Often translated as "The chapter on legal procedures" or "On (the monks at) Campā" [Norman 1983], it provides a detailed, technical treatment of monastic jurisprudence and the formal validity of communal ecclesiastical acts (*saṅghakamma*) [von Hinüber 1996]. The narrative begins at Campā when the monk Kassapagotta is maliciously accused of having committed an offense, prompting the Buddha to lay down criteria distinguishing valid procedures from invalid or discordant acts carried out by an incomplete or factional assembly; violations incur an offense of wrongdoing (*dukkaṭa*) [Entrance to the Vinaya 1983; Banerjee 1979; Horner 1966].

 Banerjee notes that the introductory narrative in the Tibetan Vinaya closely mirrors the Pali account—with the accused monk named Sde-’joms (Senajit) corresponding to Kassapagotta—though the Pali procedural discussions are more extensive [Banerjee 1979]. Complete English translations have been made by T. W. Rhys Davids and Hermann Oldenberg, I. B. Horner, and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Prebish 1994].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: san-mu-kd10 Karmavastu; xct-mu-kd10 Campeyya; lzh-mu-kd10 Campeyya; Lzh Sarv Kd10 Campeyya Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 10 Campeyya Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 10c c. Campeyya Khandhaka
- Resembling parallels: Lzh Mg Bu Pn1 Vagga 1. Upasampadā; Kd 22 Sattasatikakkhandhaka; Kd 12 Pārivāsikakkhandhaka

**Sources**

- [Frauwallner 1956] E. Frauwallner, The Earliest Vinaya and the Beginnings of Buddhist Literature (1956) — Outlined the position of Campeyyakkhandhaka in the Khandhaka sequence corresponding to Karmavastu.
- [Entrance to the Vinaya 1983] Entrance to the Vinaya: Vinayamukha Vol. 3 (1983) — Discussed the prohibition at Campā against performing saṅghakamma with incomplete attendance and the resulting dukkaṭa penalty.
- [von Hinüber 1996] Oskar von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pāli Literature (1996) — Described the text's placement in Mahāvagga, its alternative name Campeyyake vinayavatthusmiṃ, and technical legal content.
- [Horner 1966] I. B. Horner, The Book of the Discipline, Vol. VI (1966) — Confirmed the class of offense incurred in Mahāvagga IX as wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pāli Literature (1983) — Listed the text among Khandhaka chapters as 'On (the monks at) Campā'.
- [Banerjee 1979] Anukul Chandra Banerjee, Sarvāstivāda Literature (1979) — Analyzed correspondence between the Tibetan vinaya text and the Pali Campeyyakkhandhaka, noting Kassapagotta/Sde-hjoms.
- [Prebish 1994] Charles S. Prebish, A Survey of Vinaya Literature (1994) — Listed the text, its Karmavastu counterpart, and translations by Horner and Rhys Davids/Oldenberg.
- [Sung 1999] Kang-yuan Sung, Tradition and Development in the Mo-ho-sêng-ch'i-lü (1999) — Noted the reference to 'Campeyyaka vinayavatthu' in the Sattasatikakkhandhaka.
